limits: Exact-head diagnostics only. The assignment notes this head conflicts with its base; this probe does not resolve or evaluate the conflict and says nothing about the merged result.

The cluster nodes are in-process and share one system property. A relative configSetBaseDir was resolved against each node's own solr home to obtain genuinely separate per-node directories; the named configset was copied into each node's base after startup, which FileSystemConfigSetService reads from disk on demand.
The probe verifies that a named configset remains usable, not the full configset management API or every ConfigSetService operation.
The documentation-wording finding is out of scope for this gate.
Linux aarch64 and Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1+1 only.
No contributor branch was pushed and no PR comment was posted.

overlay.diff: Full new-file diff is in the evidence archive (overlay.diff); the file was deleted before release.

summary: Investigation completed at the exact head with fresh logs and JUnit XML. The focused baseline passed. A test-only probe used a relative configSetBaseDir so each in-process node resolved a distinct directory, then started SolrCloud with FileSystemConfigSetService on a base lacking _default. With solr.configset.default.confdir pointing at the real _default conf, both nodes bootstrapped _default. With the property set to a blank string, neither node created _default, and a named configset copied into each node's base remained usable (collection create, index, query, reload) in both scenarios. Existing tests contain no explicit assertion of startup bootstrap and no blank-confdir suppression case.
